title: Aim at the largest
description:
Write `aimAtLargest(values, count, target)`. It makes the caller's pointer, whose address is `target`, point at the largest of the `count` ints starting at `values`. If several are equally large, aim at the first of them. If `count` is 0, set the caller's pointer to `nullptr`.

The function returns nothing: its only result is the change to the caller's pointer.

```cpp
int scores[]{ 4, 9, 2, 9 };
int* best{ nullptr };
aimAtLargest(scores, 4, &best);   // best now points at scores[1]
```
hints: Start by setting `*target` to `nullptr`: that is the answer when there are no values.
Go through the values. If nothing is aimed at yet, or this value is bigger than the one aimed at (`**target`), aim at this one: `*target = &values[i];`.
